```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B has a buyer with budget authority (Engineering/Platform lead) and sourced paid comparables in its own category: Harness AI add-ons at $20-50/dev/month and Testhide Cloud from $49/mo. A states outright that every competitor found is free and that no paid comparable exists.",
    "A's payer is an individual developer expensing a personal tool. A's own brief calls this one of the hardest audiences to convert from free OSS, which hurts the odds of a paying customer within 90 days.",
    "Both ideas face crowded fields of indie/OSS clones. B's field also includes incumbents that charge money, which suggests willingness to pay. A's field is about seven free tools plus a free native feature in GitLab, which suggests the category is being commoditized.",
    "B has a free self-serve listing channel (GitHub Marketplace) that can take payments, plus a sourced CAC benchmark. A's paid channel is newsletter sponsorship with no conversion data behind it.",
    "B's risks are serious: trust and false negatives, cold-start data, and DPA/security review. But B's brief names them, and an advisory-only flaky-test signal is a plausible lower-trust wedge. A's core value is capped by a parity problem the brief itself calls inherently hard."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's price hypothesis ($15-20/month individual, $200/month team) rests entirely on Depot's $20/month plan. That is a hosted CI runner, a different product from a local step-through debugger, and A's brief concedes no paid comparable exists. The only direct willingness-to-pay signal is a single HN comment ('Solve this and I would pay for it').",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-low confidence. B's demand evidence is weaker than A's in one respect. One quote comes from an employee of a flaky-test vendor (Trunk) via vendor content marketing, and none of B's quotes state willingness to pay. B's six-week MVP estimate is marked unsourced. B also carries real trust and cold-start risks that could stall a first sale. The pick rests mainly on B having a budget-holding buyer and paid comparables in its category, against A's all-free market and individual buyer."
}
```
